review.scope_assessment: Reviewed the exact modified-file delta 4d7ed958...->7f28aaa5... in full (7 modified source/doc files, 10 new evidence files) against the base snapshot, plus every full file supplied for callers/constraints (production-operations.ts, isolated-backup.ts, pool-lifecycle.ts, postgres.ts, worktree.ts, the unit test file, backup-restore.ts, hold/pricing/production-guest contracts, ci.yml, .gitignore). For P2-01, confirmed the regex change from a targeted denylist (`NEXT_PUBLIC_.*(SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|RECOVERY|DATABASE)`) to a blanket `^NEXT_PUBLIC_/i` match against any nonempty value, verified the new focused test asserts rejection for both secret-sounding and neutral names (NEXT_PUBLIC_ANY_NAME), and cross-checked the supplied low-before.log (single failing assertion, exit 1, on NEXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APIKEY under the old code) against low-after.log (all 15 unit cases green after the fix) as genuine red/green evidence, further corroborated by matching lines in both local test-unit.log and the independently fetched CI test-unit.log at the exact head. For P2-02, read the actual installed embedded-postgres 18.4.0-beta.17 dist/index.js excerpts (constructor and start()) confirming start() never reads options.password (only initialise() would), which supports characterizing this as a clarity fix rather than a functional security fix; confirmed scripts/isolated-backup.ts now passes backup.auth.password into the EmbeddedPostgres constructor (matching the subsequent Pool's credential) and that tests/readiness/backup-restore.ts adds a real wrong-password Pool connection test expecting Postgres code 28P01, present in restore-review-followup.log, local test-integration-p2.log, and the independently fetched CI test-integration-p2.log at the exact head. Verified the previously missing .gitignore (`.local/` on line 2) and the new exclusion-proof.json/dependency-start-contract.md close the two 'insufficient_evidence' gaps from review-01.json (backup-directory exclusion and embedded-postgres internal behavior), cross-checked against the independently supplied CI artifact_exclusion_check (91 files, no cluster/backup paths, actual archive checked) and the exact-head CI run (34752316444, head 7f28aaa5..., base bdbb7384..., merge-tree consistent, conclusion success). Confirmed the historical CI34749426170 staff-create500 observation is still carried forward unresolved (not claimed fixed) in status.json/ADR/runbook, and that all other unrelated business/authorization/price/transfer/HOLD/wear/custody/guest/SEO/UI regressions in both local and CI logs pass unchanged. Did not and could not independently execute any code (tests_executed=false); relied on the supplied logs/CI evidence, which are internally consistent with the diff and with each other. Production/provider/device/legal/main-protection gates remain explicitly open and unaffected by this scoped correction; no new production activation, provider connection, or merge occurred or is authorized by this pass.

prior_finding_dispositions.evidence: packages/contracts/src/production-operations.ts line 28 diff replaces the narrow heuristic regex `/^NEXT_PUBLIC_.*(SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|RECOVERY|DATABASE)/i` with a blanket `/^NEXT_PUBLIC_/i` match on any nonempty value, closing the exact gap the original finding identified (NEXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APIKEY and similarly-named-but-not-matched variables). New test 'P2-01 unapproved public environment names fail closed regardless of secret-like spelling' in tests/unit/production-integration.test.ts asserts rejection for NEXT_PUBLIC_SQUARE_APIKEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_STORAGE_CREDENTIAL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNING_CERT and the deliberately non-secret-sounding NEXT_PUBLIC_ANY_NAME. low-before.log shows this exact test failing (AssertionError, missing expected exception) under the pre-fix code; low-after.log and both local/CI test-unit.log show it passing post-fix among all 15 unit cases. No functional weakening: the new check is strictly broader/more conservative (fail-closed) than the original heuristic, and existing legitimate calls (private ZAO_PRODUCTION_SECRET_METADATA only, no NEXT_PUBLIC_* set) are unaffected, consistent with the stated absence of any current NEXT_PUBLIC_* product users.

scripts/isolated-backup.ts line 33 diff replaces `password:randomBytes(24).toString('hex')` with `password:backup.auth.password`, matching the subsequent `new Pool({...backup.auth})` and removing the misleading implication that restore rotates credentials. docs/execution/production-p2-evidence/dependency-start-contract.md supplies the actual installed embedded-postgres 18.4.0-beta.17 dist/index.js source (constructor lines 85-99, start() lines 187-229) confirming start() never reads options.password (only initialise(), which restore never calls) -- corroborating the original review's characterization that this is a clarity/maintenance fix rather than a functional defect, now made consistent with the real credential rather than an inert random one. tests/readiness/backup-restore.ts adds a genuine restore-time assertion that a Pool connecting with a deliberately wrong password is rejected with Postgres code 28P01, passing in both local (restore-review-followup.log, test-integration-p2.log: 5 cases) and independently fetched CI test-integration-p2.log at the exact head. This is documentation/consistency correction, not a reproduced security defect, and no rotation/initialise semantics were introduced.
